title: Shah offers special Parliament session on SIR and EVMs, challenges Rahul Gandhi to debate
dek: Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the government is ready to convene a special session and invited the Congress leader to take up his 'vote chori' charges there.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Monday that the government is ready to convene a special session of Parliament to debate the Opposition's allegations of "vote chori" (vote theft), and challenged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to come and make his case there, according to reports by The Week and Oneindia.

Shah named three subjects he wanted debated: electronic voting machines (EVMs), the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and what he called infiltrators. He extended the same challenge to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Asking how Congress had formed state governments, including in Telangana, "if the EVMs are bad", he also said Gandhi could become prime minister only in a "mock Parliament".

The challenge came hours after Congress's "Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao" protest, part of a campaign the party launched against what it calls vote theft during the SIR. Congress general secretary K C Venugopal has said the party will keep protesting until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is removed. Gandhi has alleged that forms were manipulated during the revision. The Election Commission has rejected these claims, according to reporting on the campaign.

Congress has not formally accepted the invitation, as far as reports show. No date for any special session has been announced, and calling one requires a government decision and a summons by the President. Wording is as reported by the outlets named.
